title: A Cellar for the Portrait
premise: Sable Whitlock hosts the graveyard shift at a dying AM station, taking calls from listeners who, according to every record, died the week before. They refuse to believe in ghosts—until their childhood imaginary friend, Wren, appears on their porch exactly as they left him thirty years ago, unchanged and increasingly desperate. Wren reveals that Sable's family took something from the cellar of their childhood house in 1974: a portrait of a child who never existed, painted over a face that did. As the frost creeps inward and the dead callers grow more insistent, Sable must return to the condemned house, confront what their family buried, and decide whether loyalty to the living lie is worth more than the truth. In the end, Sable gives the portrait back to the cellar—and to the child inside it—choosing truth over belonging, and finally allowing themselves to be seen.
about_author: Theo Coldharbour is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent a decade answering phones for insomniacs, conspiracy theorists, and the occasionally impossible caller. They write horror about small towns, old houses, and the things families agree not to mention.

chapters.title: The Dead Air Shift
chapters.summary: Third-person limited POV on Sable Whitlock, hosting 'Nightline' at KOWL-AM. A caller describes her own funeral with cheerful precision; Sable assumes a prank and moves on. The emotional beat is professional detachment masking loneliness—we see how invisible Sable has made themselves, even on air.

chapters.title: Seven Callers, One Week
chapters.summary: Sable checks the obituaries against the night's call log and finds all seven callers died within the last week. POV stays with Sable as they build rational explanations—coincidence, a hoax ring, a database error. Emotional beat: denial sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: Sable arrives home to find Wren—the imaginary friend from 1974—sitting on the porch steps, ageless, wearing the same corduroy coat. He says only, 'You kept it too long.' POV: Sable, shaken into raw honesty for the first time. Beat: the impossible made domestic.

chapters.title: What Imaginary Friends Remember
chapters.summary: Over instant coffee, Wren recounts their shared childhood in Ash Hollow, filling gaps Sable had sealed. He mentions the cellar and stops himself. Sable interrogates him like a hostile guest on air. Beat: the tension between wanting answers and fearing them.

chapters.title: Obituary Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable researches the dead callers and finds they all lived near Ash Hollow or once had. One was a classmate they'd forgotten. POV shifts briefly to the classmate's widow, who heard her husband's voice on the radio and wept with relief. Beat: grief meets uncanny hope.

chapters.title: The House That Was Condemned
chapters.summary: Sable drives to the family house, boarded since 1974, and stands at the fence unable to enter. Wren waits in the passenger seat, refusing to come closer than the property line. Beat: dread of return; the past physically fenced off.

chapters.title: Mother's Version
chapters.summary: Sable visits their mother, Ruth, now sharp-tongued in a care facility. Ruth denies everything about 1974 with rehearsed smoothness, then whispers, 'Don't let it finish the pattern.' Beat: loyalty to family myth versus the crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Back at the station, frost blooms on the studio windows in branching, deliberate shapes—like veins, like a face. The dead callers begin calling together, speaking in overlapping chorus. POV: Sable, losing the anchor of routine. Beat: the supernatural becomes ambient, inescapable.

chapters.title: A Portrait of No One
chapters.summary: In a storage unit of family effects, Sable finds photographs of the cellar: crates, a covered easel, and their father's handwriting—'It goes back down.' Wren finally admits he was there in 1974, that he saw what was carried up. Beat: betrayal and tenderness tangled.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't Painted
chapters.summary: Through Wren's fragmented memory, we learn of a child who vanished in Ash Hollow before Sable was born—a girl whose name was scraped from records. The portrait in the cellar may hold her likeness, painted over. Beat: the mystery acquires a human cost.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: The station manager threatens to fire Sable after listeners complain about 'the ghost hour.' Sable broadcasts anyway, asking the dead directly what they want. The answer, in chorus: 'Bring her back.' Beat: Sable chooses the story over the job—identity shifting.

chapters.title: Ruth Breaks
chapters.summary: Second visit to Ruth, who this time tells a partial truth: in 1974, Sable's father found the portrait and hid it upstairs instead of returning it, believing ownership would protect the family. Ruth helped carry it. She has been afraid of cellars ever since. Beat: pity replacing anger.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren admits he isn't imaginary at all—he is what remains of the vanished girl's guardian, bound to whoever holds the portrait. He stayed with child-Sable because Sable needed him, but his true duty is the return. Beat: loyalty vs. truth embodied in one character.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Sable cuts the padlock on the family house and enters. Dust, cold, and the staircase down. The frost follows them indoors, climbing the walls in patterns that match the window-ferns. Beat: crossing the threshold; no way back to denial.

chapters.title: The Cellar Door
chapters.summary: Descending, Sable relives sensory memories—chalk smell, a hand-held hand. At the bottom: an empty easel frame shaped like a doorway, and scratch marks on the inside of the coal chute. Beat: claustrophobic terror and dawning comprehension.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Four
chapters.summary: A full flashback chapter, third person on young Sable and Wren: the night the portrait was carried up, the girl's voice in the walls, the parents' pact of silence. Young Sable chose not to ask questions. Beat: the origin of the lie and Sable's complicity.

chapters.title: The Chorus on Line Two
chapters.summary: Present day: the dead callers reach Sable by phone even in the cellar, no signal required. They describe their own deaths gently, then say the frost will 'write its final pattern' at first hard freeze—three nights away. Beat: deadline set; stakes made mortal.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Sable confronts Ruth one last time, offering her the chance to help return the portrait. Ruth refuses—admitting the truth would unmake the family she insists survived intact. Sable leaves alone. Beat: severing false belonging; grief and resolve.

chapters.title: The Uncovering
chapters.summary: With Wren's guidance, Sable finds the portrait hidden in the attic chimney flue: a painting of a girl whose face has been painted over with a stranger's smile. As Sable scrapes the overpainting, the frost outside recedes a single inch. Beat: act of restoration begins.

chapters.title: First Hard Freeze
chapters.summary: Climax. On the final night, Sable carries the portrait down through the house as the frost races across the floors toward the cellar door. The dead stand in the yard, patient. Wren falters at the threshold—bound to leave when the debt is paid. Beat: terror, urgency, love.

chapters.title: Returned
chapters.summary: Sable sets the portrait on the easel in the cellar and speaks the girl's recovered name aloud. The overpainting finishes dissolving; the frost writes its final pattern and stops—an ending, not a sentence. The dead callers thank Sable on the studio line, one by one, and hang up forever. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Weeks later, Sable hosts a quieter show for the living, signing off each night with the girl's name as a dedication. On the porch, no one waits—but the door is unlocked now, and Sable leaves the light on. Final beat: belonging chosen freely, identity no longer hidden.
